# PostureCheckMac

PostureCheckMac is a Ziti posture check that a device passes if it has one of the listed MAC addresses.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | posture check of type `MAC`, `/edge/management/v1/posture-checks` |
| Updated with | `PATCH`: a setting that is left out of the spec is left alone in Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/posturecheck/mac.yaml`](../../examples/posturecheck/mac.yaml):

```yaml
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostureCheckMac
metadata:
  name: registered-devices
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: registered-devices
    # Quoted, so that YAML does not read an address of digits as a number.
    # Either case and the separators ":", "-" and "." are accepted; Ziti
    # stores the addresses in lower case and without separators.
    macAddresses:
      - "0A-1B-2C-3D-4E-5F"
      - "00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e"
    roleAttributes:
      - registered-devices
```

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the posture check. |
| `macAddresses` | list of strings, required |  | `macAddresses` | MacAddresses that pass the check: a device must have one of them. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `roleAttributes` | list of strings |  | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes service policies select the posture check by, as "#attribute". |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The provider also sends `typeId: MAC`.

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## Status: `status.atProvider`

| Field | Type | What it shows |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `name` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `createdAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `id` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `macAddresses` | list of strings | MacAddresses as Ziti stores them: in lower case and without separators. |
| `roleAttributes` | list of strings | As Ziti reports it. |
| `tags` | map of strings | As Ziti reports it. |
| `typeId` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `updatedAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |

## How it behaves

- Ziti keeps the addresses as a set, in lower case and without separators. The spec may give them in either case and with `:`, `-`, `.` or spaces between the digits; the provider sends and compares them in the form Ziti stores, which is what `status.atProvider` shows.
- A posture check does nothing on its own: name it in `postureCheckRoles` of a [`ServicePolicy`](servicepolicy.md), as `@name` or by a role attribute.

## When something goes wrong

- The API server rejects the manifest: the list is empty, or an address has characters that are neither hexadecimal digits nor separators.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
